about: Capital-gains rules, versioned by financial year. Code asks for taxRules["FY2026-27"]; it never holds a rate itself. A year with no entry is not guessed: the engine either carries the latest configured year forward as a stated assumption or reports that the year is unsupported. frontend/lib/regulatory/tax_rules.json is a byte-for-byte mirror; a test fails if they drift.
disclaimer: Tax calculations are estimates for education, not tax advice. Consult a qualified tax professional for your individual tax position.

sources.title: Equity STCG 20% and LTCG 12.5% above Rs 1.25 lakh, for transfers on or after 23 Jul 2024; unchanged for 2026-27
Specified mutual fund: more than 65% in debt and money-market instruments, for FY 2025-26 onwards (Finance (No. 2) Act 2024)

unsupportedYears.FY2024-25: Rates changed on 23 Jul 2024 inside this year (STCG 15% to 20%, LTCG 10% to 12.5%, exemption Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.25 lakh), so a single set of rates would be wrong for part of it.

surcharge.note: Surcharge depends on total income, which the simulator does not know. It is applied only when you tell it your income band.
surcharge.cappedGainsNote: Equity STCG, equity LTCG and other long-term gains taxed at 12.5% carry a surcharge of at most 15%. Gains taxed at your slab rate carry the full surcharge for your band.

FY2026-27.label: FY 2026-27
FY2026-27.legalBasis: Income-tax Act, 2025 (in force from 1 Apr 2026), which re-enacts sections 111A, 112A, 112 and 50AA of the 1961 Act at the same rates

securityClassification.note: How a listed instrument is classified for tax. Equity shares and equity-oriented ETFs follow the equity rules; other listed ETFs (gold, silver, debt, liquid, international) are taxed under the 'other' rules. Intraday trades and F&O are business income, not capital gains.

mutualFunds.note: Classification comes from the scheme's AMFI category and name, then any override you set. Categories whose mix depends on the scheme are flagged and lower the confidence of the estimate.

equity.label: Equity-oriented fund
equity.detail: At least 65% of assets in domestic equity shares. Taxed under the equity rules.

specified.label: Specified mutual fund
specified.detail: More than 65% in debt and money-market instruments. Units bought on or after 1 Apr 2023 are taxed as short-term gains at your slab rate whatever the holding period.

other.label: Other mutual fund
other.detail: Neither equity-oriented nor specified. Gains are short-term at your slab rate within 24 months and 12.5% after, with no indexation and no Rs 1.25 lakh exemption.

unknown.label: Classification unknown
unknown.detail: The AMFI category does not settle the tax class. Choose one to see an estimate.

rules.reason: Gold and silver funds hold neither equity nor debt.
An overseas fund-of-funds is not domestic-equity oriented.
This index fund tracks a debt or money-market index.
A name that suggests foreign equity: not domestic-equity oriented.
A domestic equity index fund or ETF.
Arbitrage funds hold hedged equity and are taxed as equity-oriented.
Equity savings funds usually keep 65% or more in equity and arbitrage, but the scheme decides.
Most balanced-advantage funds hedge to stay above 65% equity, but the scheme decides.
Aggressive hybrid funds hold 65% to 80% in equity.
Multi-asset funds can be above or below 65% equity depending on the scheme.
Balanced hybrid funds hold 40% to 60% equity: below the equity threshold, with debt under 65%.
Conservative hybrid funds hold 75% to 90% in debt.
A domestic fund-of-funds takes the class of the funds it holds.
A diversified or sectoral equity scheme.
A debt scheme: more than 65% in debt and money-market instruments.
